Anthony Edwards’ pitch to Jonathan Kuminga to join the Timberwolves, according to Aaron Turner:

“I want you to come here and I want you to do everything you do and do it loudly. I feel where you’re coming from. I can understand what you’ve dealt with through these parts of your career and I want you to come in here and be Jonathan Kuminga.”

Full quote by NBA agent @arockturner20 on the latest episode of The KOC Show: “Ant was a massive part of this whole thing because he said, ‘Listen, we’re gonna guard. Everybody’s going to guard.” Offensively, one of the biggest things Ant and Chris Finch said to him: ‘This whole thing of JK is a role player’ and all this stuff that’s been talked about, that was not the pitch. The pitch was, ‘Hey JK, we want you to come here and be the guy that we had to play against in the playoffs. Like, we want that dude. Like, we’re not asking you to go be something else. We’re asking you to be yourself. Now, are we going to have to all sacrifice and blend together our games? For sure.’”

“But this whole thing of like, oh, he has to adapt. No. Ant, who is as unselfish of a star as you could imagine and super secure with who he is. His whole thing was, look, ‘I want you to come here and I want you to do everything you do and do it loudly. I feel where you’re coming from. I can understand what you’ve dealt with through these parts of your career and I want you to come in here and be Jonathan Kuminga.’”

“And that was the pitch from Chris Finch as well of like, look, ‘we’re all going to guard, and you know, again, everybody here on this team will have to sacrifice. Everybody’s going to have to make sure that they’re making the right play and not necessarily getting caught up in my turn, your turn.’ And I’m sure Chris Finch will figure that out. When you have a great team, people have to sacrifice. But the pitch was not come here and oh, you got to be this quote unquote, whatever you want to call it, role player. The thing was, hey, come here, be you. We’re all going to have to sacrifice. But if it’s about winning, and it’s always going to be about winning, and that’s the most important thing, this thing has a chance to really work. And you know, Ant having reached out like that, Chris Finch following up, Tim Connelly following up, Alex Rodriguez following up, it was very aligned in the pitch and it made a lot of sense and it resonated with him and me.”

Aaron Turner on Jonathan Kuminga’s role with the Minnesota Timberwolves:

“The role is whatever's needed to win. That's the role. It's not this box or that box. Some nights it might be this. Some nights it might be that. Depending on the matchup, depending on the team. Give your heart and soul to this team. Be in this moment. Enjoy it. And then everything else will follow how it's supposed to. And everybody who says whatever they want to say, we'll see where that lands. But I have a pretty good feeling if JK is able to stay healthy and embrace this moment, which I know he's excited for, let’s see what happens.“

The experiment was an immediate success, starting off with a 84-43 win, and following that with a 68-3 blowout. Both were against non-NCAA opponents, but gave hope that Presbyterian might have introduced the biggest change to the game of college football since the forward pass.

They lost their last 9 games and Kelley was let go. But oh what a season it was.

The Warriors’ dynasty was built on Steph, Klay, and Draymond, but their recent draft record and roster moves read like a massive timeline of missed opportunities 😳

Back in 2020, Minnesota offered the No. 1 pick to Golden State. The Dubs passed, the Wolves nabbed Anthony Edwards, and Golden State settled on James Wiseman at No. 2. 

To make matters worse, Jalen Rose revealed the Warriors actually told LaMelo Ball they’d take him before backing out at the last second. 

Then came Tyrese Haliburton. Bob Myers openly admitted the front office wrestled with selecting him after a killer workout, only to stick with Wiseman while Haliburton went on to become an All-NBA guard.

The 2021 draft brought even more internal debate. Golden State's coaching staff and scouts wanted Franz Wagner at No. 7, but Joe Lacob pushed for Jonathan Kuminga. 

Fast forward to now: Wagner is an established, max-contract cornerstone in Orlando, while Kuminga is already off the team.

To top it all off, Golden State completely botched their pursuit of LeBron James this summer. Even with Draymond opting out to help clear room this summer and reported mutual interest, LeBron stunned the league by signing with the Sixers instead.

Between passing on Edwards, LaMelo, Haliburton, and Wagner, the Kuminga standoff, and failing to pull off the LeBron blockbuster, the Warriors' transition era is starting to look like a running reel of what-ifs.
